hyps.why: Replacing a removed direct input-to-output edge with a skip adds a gradient path, a much larger gain than swapping it for any existing op.
Adding a 3x3 conv where the edge was absent gains more than replacing an op that already contributes.
With edge 4 removed, node 3's inputs depend more on edge 5, so a strong op there matters more.
Turning a dead edge into a 3x3 conv adds capacity and a new path into the output.
Reconnecting node 1 with a conv enables its downstream edges, which gives a larger gain than swapping among existing ops.
Removing a conv edge into the output loses much more accuracy than removing a pool or an already-weak edge.
Deleting the direct skip removes the key shortcut path, which hurts more than deleting other ops.
When the direct 0->3 edge is absent, a skip on 1->3 supplies the missing shortcut-like path.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 carries no signal, so an op on edge 1->2 has almost no effect.
A direct skip already provides a good path, so extra conv capacity on another branch yields diminishing returns.
